faq.q: Does it post the report anywhere?
faq.a: Only where you choose. Husn assembles and surfaces the report but never posts, edits, or moves anything in Jira, Slack, or your documents on its own. You stay in control of what gets sent.

faq.q: How current is each report?
faq.a: It reflects recent activity, not the last standup. Because Husn keeps its underlying view current, the report you generate matches the work as it stands when you create it.

title: Portfolio risk management software
metaDescription: Software to manage risk across a portfolio of programs. Husn reads Jira, Slack, and docs and surfaces portfolio risk with sources and affected teams.
heroSubheadline: Across a portfolio of programs, risk is a tooling problem as much as a judgment one. Husn reads every program and keeps the portfolio view of risk current without a weekly assembly exercise.
primaryPain: Portfolio risk software often turns into a place to record risk after the fact rather than find it as it forms. Program managers enter what they already know, so the tool reflects their attention, and whatever they did not have time to read stays invisible at the portfolio level.
painBullets: The portfolio view is only as good as what each program manager remembered to enter, so coverage is uneven by design.
Cross program risk, where one program's slip threatens another, is exactly what manual entry tends to miss.
Refreshing the portfolio view is a periodic project in itself, so it is current only for a day or two each cycle.
whyHard: It depends on entry. A tool that records what people type reflects their bandwidth, not the full state of the portfolio.
It misses the seams. Cross program risk lives between programs, where no single program manager is responsible for spotting it.
It is effortful to refresh. Keeping a portfolio view current by hand competes with the actual work of running the programs.
howHusnHelps: Husn reads each program's Jira, Slack, and docs and identifies risk as it forms, so the portfolio view is found, not just entered.
It connects risk across programs, surfacing when one program's change raises another's exposure, with the affected teams named.
The portfolio view stays current on its own, so it reflects the work continuously rather than only just after a refresh.

items.text: A delivery date in one program slipped, raising risk for a dependent program that has not re-planned.
A program's scope grew materially since the last portfolio review, with no updated forecast.

faq.q: How is this different from a portfolio risk register?
faq.a: A register records risk that someone entered. Husn finds risk as it forms by reading each program's tools, so the portfolio view reflects the actual state of the work rather than what people had time to log.

faq.q: Can it see risk across programs?
faq.a: Yes. Husn connects related risk between programs, so when one program's change raises another's exposure, it surfaces that link with the affected teams named, which single program reports miss.

faq.q: Does it write to our program tools?
faq.a: No. Husn is read only across every program. It never posts, edits, or moves anything in Jira, Slack, or your documents. It reads, reconciles, and surfaces.

faq.q: How current is the portfolio view?
faq.a: Continuous. Husn keeps the view current by reading the work as it changes, so the portfolio reflects today rather than the last manual refresh before a review.
